correctness.rationale: The prefix-constrained Gaussian orthoscheme q1=s=h², r_k=sum_{j<=k}q_j>=k has minimal feasible closed prefix sequence r*_k=max(k,s), q*_j=r*_j-r*_{j-1}. Abel summation against ordered squares makes the quadratic exponent >= the q* exponent, yielding the exact Gaussian supremum. After ordered-square change, Psi_n(sqrt s) equals an expectation of a strictly decreasing positive Jacobian factor times a nonincreasing exponential; hence it decreases, with derivative jumps at s=2,...,n from newly active (z_k²-z_{k+1}²). For s>=n, integrate z2..zn to get Psi=n2^{n-1}Gamma(n/2)/(pi^{n/2}h^{n-1}). The cited Rogers/Karasev orthoscheme flag-area contraction transfers the Gaussian comparison to each facet under full affine-face-distance hypotheses; summation gives the surface bound. Direct radial Jacobian yields sharp high-height truncated-cube infimum. In n=2, elementary angular Gaussian integration and the stated trapezoid give all intermediate h equality. Independently checked the n=2 piecewise formula and threshold numeric samples and the algebraic q* prefix logic.
